changes.motivation: swayrd was exiting silently without registering as a systemd failure — existing startLimitBurst/startLimitIntervalSec config was dead without a Restart= directive, so the unit would go inactive (dead) rather than failed, making crashes invisible to systemctl --user --failed and hard to diagnose via journalctl.
changes.summary: Added Restart=always and RestartSec to the swayrd systemd user service in modules/common/sway/default.nix. Now failed exits trigger restarts, and after hitting the burst limit (3 restarts in 15s) the unit properly enters failed state with full journal logs captured.

problems: startLimitBurst and startLimitIntervalSec were already set on the swayrd service, creating a misleading impression that restart limiting was functional, when in fact no Restart= directive was present so systemd never attempted a restart and the limit settings had no effect.
Branch and issue name used 'sayrd' but the actual service/program is 'swayrd', causing unnecessary search confusion at the start of the session.
